response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate that integrates the decisive LTBP2 genotype with the Weill-Marchesani phenotype, making it the most complete and specific diagnosis. R4 is the strongest independent differential because of tall stature, long fingers, and lens dislocation, but it is contradicted by normal serial echocardiograms, negative family history, and LTBP2 rather than FBN1 variants. R2 lacks exfoliation-specific findings and is contradicted by the open angle and genetic result; R3 has no raw support beyond nonspecific hypermobility; R1 is subsumed by C1 because it omits the causal LTBP2 variants.

rejected.why: Pseudoexfoliation is unsupported: no exfoliation material is described, the angle is open, and the LTBP2 genotype points to a genetic ectopia lentis/glaucoma syndrome.
Ehlers-Danlos has no raw support; hypermobility alone is nonspecific and there is no skin/connective tissue or genetic confirmation.
Correct syndrome but incomplete; it lacks the decisive LTBP2 etiology that C1 adds, so it is subsumed by the champion.
